claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 7 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 7 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or somewhere to live)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his expenses regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. To determine if your contributions meet the requirements for Child Benefit eligibility, I need to understand more about them.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (for example, weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Now I need to ask a couple more questions:

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Is Alex's mum (or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is there any reason Alex might be in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period, or any other unusual circumstances I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually - Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that important detail. I need to understand this situation better as it affects eligibility.

**How long has Alex been in local authority care, and does he spend any regular time at home with you (for example, does he come home for at least 24 hours a week, or spend weekends or longer periods with you)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for about 10 weeks now, and no, he doesn't come home to stay with me - he's there full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask one more question about this situation:

**Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with his mum, or does he spend any regular time staying with her (such as 2 nights in a row each week or 7 days or more in a row)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't spend that amount of time with his mum either. He's at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While Alex is 7 years old (under 16) and you live in the UK and make regular financial contributions of £50 per week towards his upkeep, the key issue is that Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 10 weeks.

Under the Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into care for **more than 8 weeks**, you're usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit. There is an exception to this rule if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you, but since Alex is in the care home full-time and doesn't spend regular time at home with either you or his mum, this exception doesn't apply.

I understand this may be disappointing news, especially given that you're contributing financially to Alex's upkeep. If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he begins spending at least 24 hours a week at home, or 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home - you may be able to claim Child Benefit at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
